ordered_replacements.old: Spillover-compensation effects varied across six segmentation methods, tissue regions and cell types, with no consistent improvement across metrics. We compared four clustering methods—Leiden, FlowSOM, SpatialSort, and PIXIE—against reference annotations. We evaluated four large language models (LLMs)—GPT-5.6-Sol, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, and DeepSeek V4 Pro—for automated annotation of cluster-level marker-expression profiles. Across clustering and LLM annotation, performance depended on the method, model, cell type, tissue region, and evaluation metric. In an end-to-end Leiden–Claude pipeline, 55.93% of cells matched the reference label. Adding labeled reference profiles increased reference agreement in 15 of 16 method-model comparisons.
ordered_replacements.new: Spillover-compensation effects varied across six segmentation methods, tissue regions and cell types, with no consistent improvement across metrics. We compared Leiden, FlowSOM, SpatialSort and PIXIE against reference annotations using the refreshed frozen primary partitions. The 47-marker FlowSOM and SpatialSort updates produced metric-dependent changes in reference agreement. [[INSERT VERIFIED SUMMARY OF THE REFRESHED FOUR-MODEL ANNOTATION BENCHMARK, PAIRED INPUT COMPARISON AND REPEATED-CALL CONSISTENCY RESULTS.]] Separate historical reference-assisted analyses were retained with their original models, partitions and scoring protocols.

ordered_replacements.old: Each 21-label benchmark cluster profile contained 12 high-ranked and eight low-ranked markers. Each entry included the marker name, its transformed mean expression within the cluster, and its difference from the mean across all B004 cells expressed in units of the standard deviation across those cells. Prompts also provided task context and allowed 21 labels in total: 20 cell-type labels plus Noise (Supplementary Note 1). The prompt requested exactly one allowed label per cluster and a JSON-object response.
ordered_replacements.new: [Author update note: The 47-marker clustering results are complete. The refreshed annotation methods are drafted for the planned rerun. Annotation outcomes, model bindings and costs will be filled from verified outputs. Figures marked historical retain their original predictions and values.] Each refreshed cluster profile contained means for all 47 protein markers. We compared these means alone with identical means plus the fractions of cells whose processed marker values were strictly above zero. Means were calculated after arcsinh(processed expression/5) and standardized using the existing four B004 training regions. Fractions were calculated from processed measurements before transformation or standardization. Marker and cluster order, means, numerical encoding, vocabulary, batching and model settings were matched within each pair. Prompts requested exactly one of the original 28 labels, including Noise, for each cluster and a JSON-object response. Neither arm received labeled reference profiles, clustering-method names, neighborhood information or tools.

ordered_replacements.old: GPT-5.6-Sol, Claude Opus 5, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview and DeepSeek V4 Pro each annotated the four clustering outputs in the 21-label benchmark, producing 16 prediction sets. The 179 contributing calls requested high reasoning effort. We retained recorded model identifiers, provider routes, settings, prompts, response handling, usage and costs without inferring missing metadata. The separate all-marker benchmark supplied all 45 means and positive fractions. Supplementary Note 2 distinguishes these experiments and documents execution and failure handling.
ordered_replacements.new: Four model families from OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and DeepSeek annotated the four frozen clustering partitions in each marker-input arm. [[INSERT VERIFIED MODEL IDS, PROVIDER ROUTES, SUPPORTED HIGH-REASONING SETTINGS, TOKEN BUDGETS AND EXECUTION DATES.]] The design requested five fresh repetitions per arm, model and method, totaling 160 annotation sets. Batches contained at most 75 clusters. The 1,128 occupied primary clusters specified 640 initial physical requests before eligible transport retries. Arm order was deterministically counterbalanced. We recorded each physical request, response, usage and observed cost once, even when its predictions supported more than one declared analysis. The historical 21-label benchmark and reference-assisted controls were retained separately.

ordered_replacements.old: Across the 16 clustering-method–LLM combinations in the 21-label benchmark, cell-level reference agreement ranged from 31.3% to 55.9%, or 62.3% to 87.4% of the cluster-majority upper bound (Figure 3B–C). These agreement measures across all B004 cells include the 4.77% Noise reference class. Performance varied by method-model pair and cell type. No model or clustering method was uniformly best across all comparisons. These 21-label benchmark results used the harmonized reference labels described in Section 2.5 and the allowed-label vocabulary described in Section 2.10 and Supplementary Note 1. The controlled B004 and donor-transfer analyses used different cell-type label lists, so their scores should not be treated as directly equivalent to the 21-label benchmark scores.
ordered_replacements.new: Across the 16 clustering-method–model combinations, we reported equal-weighted agreement across the two existing B004 test regions and fixed-28-label macro-F1 as the mean and sample SD across five fresh repetitions. Missing or invalid predictions remained errors in the planned denominator. [[INSERT VERIFIED AGREEMENT AND MACRO-F1 RANGES, MODEL/METHOD CONTRASTS AND DELIVERY COVERAGE FROM THE NEW RUN.]] These repeatedly examined B004 data describe computational variation rather than new donor replication. The historical 21-label benchmark and the separate donor-transfer experiment used different vocabularies and settings and were analyzed separately.
